failure.message: the load is still signing its queues after 600s

cause: The chaos harness signs the entire upper load window before publishing readiness. Long deployment windows multiply signing work and retained transaction bytes even when recovery ends early.

change.scope: Plain-transfer chaos loads only. Other workloads and ordinary performance loads retain full pre-signing.
change.batch_bound: ceil(4096 / senders) transfers per sender; at most current, one queued and one signing batch.
invariants: Identical signed bytes, hashes, sender rotation and per-sender nonces
Existing total plan, pacing, workload rates, recovery deadlines and receipt checks
First batch signs before readiness; each refill publishes receipt expectations before submitting
Signer errors and premature channel closure fail the run, never count as normal exhaustion
Dropping the receiver stops a blocked producer after at most its current batch
Refill waits are logged so CI can distinguish signing starvation from runtime backpressure
change.memory_limit: Signed bytes are bounded independently of duration; receipt/order evidence still grows with the traffic actually observed.

validation.negative_control: Removing the batch bound fails the first-batch assertion: 8198 transactions instead of 4096.
controls: Full presigning and batched streams match bytes/hash/order across multiple batches
Ordinary performance preparation still signs its full plan
Feed-before-ack and ack-before-feed preserve receipt identity checks
Nonce/block ordering spans initial and refilled expectations
Late nonce overflow and unexpected producer loss cannot end successfully
Run-level signer failure writes no passing report
Dropping a consumer releases its producer

impact: Test harness only. No product runtime, service wiring, production idle policy, shard count or case list changes.
limitations: Distributed signing/pacing, carry and node-replacement recovery still require fresh CI. A lower offered rate is not evidence of a fix.
The global runner contention and deployed performance regressions remain unresolved.
The benchmark stream keeps fully presigned inputs but shares error propagation; final-source client performance validation remains required.
